settings.gg4q0_tafLQ_text: 3. Your dog chews less – or avoids chew bones
settings.ggA_9fBzkhA_text:
Did your dog used to love chewing but suddenly leaves chew bones untouched?
This is a common sign that something in their mouth is hurting.
Dogs don’t tell us in the same way humans do – they change their behavior to avoid pain.

If your dog chews carefully, only on one side, or simply loses interest in bones or toys they usually love – this is a clear warning sign.
📌 Pay attention to these small signals. They matter.

settings.ggcksXQNDDT_text: 7. Your dog seems down or loses their appetite
settings.gggEKY2pbzl_text:
Dogs are experts at hiding pain – but behavioral changes are often the first sign that something isn’t right.

If your dog suddenly eats more slowly, plays less, becomes withdrawn, or generally seems low – it could be oral discomfort causing the change.

It’s easy to think, “She’s just tired today” – but if this continues for several days or happens repeatedly, you should check their mouth health.

📌 Even one sore tooth can make daily life difficult. Small signals – big meaning.

settings.gg7Imo_G0Kv_text:
When bacteria are left to sit on teeth, they first form a soft, invisible layer – plaque.
If ignored, it hardens into tartar – and that’s when the problems really start.

You may have noticed a yellow or brown line along the teeth, especially towards the back of the mouth.
This isn’t just a cosmetic issue – it’s a sign that bacteria have already taken hold.
The longer it stays, the harder it is to remove. Tartar becomes a hiding place for bacteria that cause bad odor, irritation, and gum inflammation.


📌 Plaque starts it – tartar locks it in. Act before it becomes serious.

settings.gg5dmRdf7vT_text: 5. Your dog pulls away when you try to check their mouth
settings.ggUe12aoVBe_text:
If you try to look at their teeth and your dog turns their head, stiffens up, or backs away – it could be more than just “not wanting to.”
Many dogs don’t like having their mouths handled – but if the mouth feels “off limits”, it can be due to pain or discomfort.

And it’s not just hard for your dog – many owners feel guilty, saying: “I want to check, but he won’t let me – and I don’t know how to help.”
📌 You’re not alone. There is help available that both you and your dog can handle.

settings.ggQwwy5lZMR_text: 1. Bad breath – that doesn’t go away
settings.ggxQYNnHwh8_text:
A healthy dog’s mouth should not smell bad. If your dog’s breath often smells sour, rotten, or like “old dishcloth,” it’s not something you should ignore.

Many owners get used to the smell or think it’s “just old age” – but in fact, bad breath is often the first sign of bacterial buildup and gingivitis.
📌 This isn’t about cosmetics – it’s about your dog’s health.
If you find yourself pulling away when your dog wants to cuddle – take it seriously.

settings.gguXA7k6ota_text:
Healthy gums should be light pink, smooth, and not sensitive. But if they are red, appear swollen, or start bleeding when touched – it’s almost always a sign of inflammation.

This irritation is obvious – even if your dog tries to hide the discomfort.
If left untreated, the inflammation can spread down to the tooth root and lead to tooth loss, pain, and bloodstream infections.

🔎 Fact: Did you know that 80% of all dogs over the age of 3 have some form of dental problem?

settings.ggXczlABFYJ_text: 6. Your dog drools more than usual
